suppress.notes: org.hdrhistogram:HdrHistogram is pulled in transitively via Micrometer (used by Spring Boot Actuator metrics); it is not a directly declared dependency. Both CVEs affect HdrHistogram up to 2.2.2, are rated LOW (VulDB CVSS 4.0 1.9 / CVSS 3.1 3.3, vector AV:L requiring local access), and are officially DISPUTED for lack of a crossed security boundary. Neither is exploitable here: (1) CVE-2026-14683 (CWE-400/CWE-789) is uncontrolled memory allocation in AbstractHistogram.decodeFromCompressedByteBuffer, reachable only when decoding an attacker-controlled compressed histogram byte buffer with a manipulated lengthOfCompressedContents. This service never deserialises/decodes external histogram data; Micrometer only encodes its own internally-produced metrics. (2) CVE-2026-14686 is an incorrect comparison / improper input validation in DoubleHistogram.recordValue ("Range Check"), reachable only when recording attacker-controlled values through that API, which this service does not expose. There is currently NO fixed release (all versions up to 2.2.2 are affected and the project has not responded), so pinning is not an option. REMOVE this suppression once a fixed HdrHistogram release is published and adopted transitively by Micrometer.

TEMPORARY suppression. CVE-2026-53914 is an unsafe-deserialization flaw (CWE-502) in the JetBrains Kotlin build-cache metadata, affecting the Kotlin toolchain before 2.4.20. This project currently uses Kotlin 2.4.10 and cannot yet upgrade because the fixed release (2.4.20) is not available in our repositories. Not exploitable here: (1) The Kotlin artifacts (kotlin-stdlib*, kotlin-reflect) are declared compileOnly and are NOT shipped in the published library jar, so consumers of this library are unaffected. (2) The flaw is build-time only and requires an attacker to plant malicious metadata in the local Kotlin/Gradle build cache. The vendor (JetBrains) scores it 6.7 with AV:L/AC:H/PR:H (local access, high privilege, high attack complexity); NVD's over-broad 9.8 AV:N enrichment does not reflect the actual attack path. Our build cache is local to the CI/dev environment and is not attacker-controlled. REMOVE this suppression and upgrade to Kotlin >= 2.4.20 once that release is published.

CVE-2026-19880 is a path traversal in logback-classic: an MDC value flows unsanitised through MDCBasedDiscriminator into a nested FileAppender path, letting an attacker who controls that MDC value (e.g. via an HTTP header) write log files outside the intended directory. It affects logback 0.9.14 through 1.6.2, so the 1.5.38 we resolve is in range. It is managed by the Spring Boot BOM (Boot 4.1.1 sets logback.version = 1.5.38). There is NO fix on the 1.5.x line: 1.5.38 is the latest release on it and the only fixed release is 1.6.3, on a different (and now the only actively maintained) release line. Logback's own release notes state "the 1.5.x series is now considered legacy", so a backport is unlikely. Upstream describes 1.6.x as a drop-in replacement for 1.5.x, and its one documented caveat (removal of Janino-based conditionals) does not affect us as no logback config here uses them. Even so, overriding logback.version is not a change we can make blind: Spring Boot 4.1.1 is not tested against 1.6.x, and logback has broken binary compatibility within a patch release before (1.5.7 changed ContextBase#getConfigurationLock()'s return type from Object to ReentrantLock, causing NoSuchMethodError in Boot's LogbackConfigurator on startup). The upgrade therefore needs a deliberate version override plus a startup and regression test, tracked separately. Not exploitable here: the vulnerable code path requires SiftingAppender / MDCBasedDiscriminator feeding a nested FileAppender. This repo declares no SiftingAppender, no discriminator and no logging.file/logging.path configuration anywhere. Under the jsonLogging profile used in deployed environments, logback-spring.xml declares only a ConsoleAppender writing JSON to stdout. Under the !jsonLogging profile (local runs), and in logback-test.xml (test scope), Spring Boot's org/springframework/boot/logging/logback/base.xml is included, which does attach a RollingFileAppender, but it writes to the static ${java.io.tmpdir}/spring.log path with no MDC or discriminator involvement. MDC values (correlationId, taken from the x-correlation-id HTTP header or SQS message header, plus requestId and messageId) are request-influenced but only ever reach the JSON encoder or a pattern layout, never a filesystem path. REMOVE this suppression when we move to the logback 1.6.x line (ideally when a Spring Boot BOM manages it), and revisit immediately if a SiftingAppender or an MDC-driven file appender path is added.

CVE-2026-47838 is an X.509 certificate CN parsing flaw in Spring Security's SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor, which can cause the wrong username to be read and allow user impersonation. Not applicable here for two independent reasons: (1) Already fixed in our version. This service resolves Spring Security 7.1.1 via the Spring Boot 4.1.1 BOM. The advisory (https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47838) states it is "a continuation of CVE-2026-22747, which addressed this same issue for Spring Security 7.0.x", so the 7.x line was patched first. Affected versions stop at 6.5.10 / 6.4.17 / 6.3.17 / 5.8.26 / 5.7.24; 7.x is not affected. (2) The vulnerable code path is unused. SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor only applies to X.509 client-certificate authentication. This service authenticates with JWT bearer tokens via spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server and configures no X.509/mTLS authentication. Note also that VMware score this 6.8 rather than NVD's 8.1, because the extractor sits behind the pre-authentication flow and exploitation "presupposes a compromise of that upstream trust". REMOVE this suppression if dependency-check stops reporting it, or revisit if this service ever adopts X.509 client-certificate authentication.

FALSE POSITIVE: we are already on a fixed version. CVE-2026-47842 is a deterministic AES/CBC encryption flaw in Spring Security's AesBytesEncryptor (all-zero IV). The advisory (https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47842) lists 7.1.0 as the only affected release on the 7.1.x line, and this service resolves Spring Security 7.1.1 via the Spring Boot 4.1.1 BOM. Dependency-check still reports it because the CVE is in "Awaiting Analysis" state with no CPE version ranges published, so there is no machine-readable "fixed at 7.1.1" boundary to match on. REMOVE this suppression once dependency-check stops reporting it.
